\begin{theorem}[Exchange symmetry of correlated Gaussian measure]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure_swap}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure_swap}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianReflection}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $\rho\in[-1,1]$. The joint law of a standard
Gaussian vector and its coordinatewise $\rho$-correlated Gaussian partner is invariant
under exchanging the two vectors.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Isometric invariance of correlated Gaussian measure]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure_isometry}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure_isometry}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianIsometry}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $Q$ be a linear isometry
of Euclidean $\mathbb R^n$. The joint law of a standard Gaussian vector and its
coordinatewise $\rho$-correlated Gaussian partner is unchanged when $Q$ is applied to
both vectors.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Almost everywhere invariance of Gaussian noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_congr_ae}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_congr_ae}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianEndpoint}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$
agree almost everywhere under the product standard Gaussian measure. Their images under
the Gaussian noise operator at parameter $\rho$ also agree almost everywhere under that
measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian noise at full correlation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_one}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$. Gaussian noise of
correlation $1$ leaves $f$ unchanged: $T_1f=f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian noise at zero correlation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_zero}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_zero}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a real-valued function on $\mathbb
R^n$, and let $\gamma$ be the product of $n$ standard Gaussian probability measures.
At correlation parameter $0$, the Gaussian noise operator is the constant function whose
value is the integral of $f$ with respect to $\gamma$: for every $x\in\mathbb R^n$,
$(T_0f)(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n} f\,d\gamma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian noise preserves the integral]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussianNoise}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussianNoise}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianEndpoint}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb
R$ be integrable with respect to the product standard Gaussian measure. Define $(T_\rho
f)(x)=\mathbb E[f(\rho x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,Y)]$, where $Y$ has that product standard
Gaussian law. Then $\mathbb E[(T_\rho f)(X)]=\mathbb E[f(X)]$ for $X$ with the same law.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability under correlated Gaussian measure]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_correlatedGaussianMeasure_mul}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_correlatedGaussianMeasure_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure_fst, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure_snd}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\gamma_n$ be the product of $n$ standard Gaussian
measures on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $\rho\in[-1,1]$. Form a pair $(X,Y)$ by taking
independent vectors $U,V$ with law $\gamma_n$ and setting $X=U$ and $Y=\rho
U+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,V$; denote the law of $(X,Y)$ by $\mu_\rho$. If $f,g:\mathbb
R^n\to\mathbb R$ each belong to $L^2(\gamma_n)$, then $(x,y)\mapsto f(x)g(y)$ is
integrable with respect to $\mu_\rho$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Integration under correlated Gaussian measure]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_correlatedGaussianMeasure}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_correlatedGaussianMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_correlatedGaussianMeasure_mul, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_correlatedGaussianMeasure_of_integrable}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\ge0$, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ each belong to
$L^2(\gamma_n)$, where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Form a
pair $(X,Y)$ by taking independent $X,W\sim\gamma_n$ and setting $Y=\rho
X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,W$. Then
\[
\int f(x)g(y)\,d\mathcal L(X,Y)(x,y)=\int f(x)\left(\int g\bigl(\rho
x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,w\bigr)\,d\gamma_n(w)\right)d\gamma_n(x),
\]
where $\mathcal L(X,Y)$ is the resulting joint distribution.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Additivity of Gaussian noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_add}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_add}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianNoise_integrand}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$
be integrable under the product standard Gaussian measure. The Gaussian noise operator
at parameter $\rho$ sends $f+g$ to the pointwise sum of its values on $f$ and $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Homogeneity of Gaussian noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_const_mul}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_const_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, $\rho,c\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$. The
Gaussian noise operator at parameter $\rho$ sends $cf$ to $c$ times its value on $f$,
pointwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian noise contraction in $L^p$]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_contract}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_contract}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_integral_prod_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianEndpoint}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $p$ be an extended nonnegative
real number with $1\le p$. If $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belongs to $L^p$ under the
product standard Gaussian measure, then its Gaussian noise image at parameter $\rho$ has
$L^p$ seminorm at most that of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be integrable with
respect to standard Gaussian measure $\gamma_n$. As $\rho$ approaches $1$ from below,
the $L^1(\gamma_n)$ norm of $T_\rho f-f$ tends to zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian noise on multilinear polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_multilinear}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_multilinear}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussian_affine_monomial, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussian_affine_monomial, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F$ assign a real coefficient $F(S)$ to each subset
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $x\in\mathbb R^n$. Define
$P_F(z)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}z_i$. Then Gaussian noise of
correlation $\rho$ satisfies
\[T_\rho P_F(x)=P_F(\rho x).\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Noise average of a Gaussian indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_indicator_eq_averaged}
\proofsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p004-b001}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_indicator_eq_averaged}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, and let $\theta\in[0,\pi]$.
For $x\in\mathbb R^n$, the Gaussian noise operator with correlation $\cos\theta$ applied
to the indicator of $A$ equals
\[\int_{\mathbb R^n}1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y),\]
where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{theorem}
